vision_question: When will DT fusion deliver grid-parity LCOE at commercial scale?

feasibility.rationale: HTS magnets and the 2024 US regulatory clarification have lifted three capabilities into the 70s. Tritium breeding remains the binding constraint — no test blanket has demonstrated TBR > 1 at scale yet. Plant economics is the second drag: FOAK $/kW estimates remain in the $10-25k band.

capabilities.name: Tritium breeding ratio > 1
capabilities.description: Self-sufficient tritium production from lithium blankets at TBR ≥ 1.05 across the plant fuel cycle.
capabilities.rationale: DT plants consume ~150 g/MW-thermal-year. External CANDU tritium supply (~25 kg total commercial inventory) is far below first-plant needs. Without breeding, no fusion economy is viable.

score.rationale: No test blanket has demonstrated TBR > 1 at scale. ITER TBM modules slated 2035+; ARC FLiBe concept paper-only.

capabilities.name: Steady-state plasma confinement
capabilities.description: Sustained Q > 5 net energy gain at commercial duty cycle (>50%) without disruptions.
capabilities.rationale: Without sustained burn, fusion is a science experiment, not a power plant. NIF demonstrated Q > 1 at single-shot in 2022; tokamaks have not.

score.rationale: SPARC commissioning 2026E targets Q > 10 in pulses. Disruption mitigation still open.

capabilities.name: First-wall + structural materials
capabilities.description: Plasma-facing materials surviving > 5 FPY of 14 MeV neutron flux without unacceptable swelling/embrittlement.
capabilities.rationale: Wall replacement frequency drives capex amortization. ITER conventional wall: ~2 FPY. Commercial plants need 5+ FPY for credible economics.

score.rationale: RAFM steels at TRL 5; ODS / SiC composites at TRL 3-4. Liquid-wall concepts (FLiBe, lithium) gaining attention.

capabilities.name: High-field HTS magnets
capabilities.description: REBCO-based superconducting magnets at 12-20T field, > 1 km tape per magnet, at industrial cost.
capabilities.rationale: High field shrinks plant size as 1/B⁴. CFS SPARC's 20T HTS magnet test (2021) was the breakthrough that revived private fusion.

score.rationale: CFS magnet validated at full field 2021. REBCO tape supply doubling but still concentrated (Faraday, AMSC, Fujikura).

capabilities.name: Plant economics — LCOE crossover
capabilities.description: FOAK and NOAK plants converging on LCOE competitive with grid + carbon ($80-120/MWh).
capabilities.rationale: Even if physics works, fusion is irrelevant unless LCOE crosses grid + carbon. FOAK estimates $15-25k/kW_e cap; learning rate uncertain.

score.rationale: Lindley et al. 2023: FOAK $10-25k/kW. CFS pilot business case targets $100/MWh by NOAK; not yet validated.

capabilities.name: Regulatory pathway clarity
capabilities.description: NRC + IAEA clear, predictable licensing pathway distinct from fission Part 50/52.
capabilities.rationale: Pre-2024 fusion was regulatory limbo. NRC's 2024 ruling treats fusion as Part 30 byproduct material — order-of-magnitude faster licensing than fission.

score.rationale: NRC Part 30 framework (April 2024) is a tailwind. UK STEP, KR K-DEMO pathways also clearer than before.

capabilities.name: REBCO tape + Be / Li supply
capabilities.description: Industrial supply of REBCO tape (HTS), beryllium (multiplier), and lithium-6 (breeder) at fusion-scale demand.
capabilities.rationale: First plant needs ~1000 km of REBCO + hundreds of tons of Be / Li-6. Today's REBCO production: ~500 km/yr globally.

score.rationale: Faraday + AMSC capacity expansions announced; Be supply still concentrated in US + Kazakhstan.

capabilities.name: Fusion engineering workforce
capabilities.description: Plasma physicists, neutronics engineers, fusion-trained operators at the scale of 10-20 commercial plants.
capabilities.rationale: Today the global fusion workforce is ~5000; commercial-scale deployment needs 10x that. Pipeline is academia + national labs.

score.rationale: Private fusion companies hiring aggressively; university programs expanding (MIT, Oxford, KAIST).

capabilities.name: Grid integration + dispatchability
capabilities.description: Fusion plants delivering baseload + dispatchable power; HV interconnection + grid services.
capabilities.rationale: Mature technology — fusion plants look like any large thermal generator from the grid's perspective. Engineering, not invention.

score.rationale: No fusion-specific blockers; standard utility-scale interconnection processes.

dependencies.rationale: Higher field enables smaller plant footprint + better confinement.
Wall integrity is a precondition for sustained burn.
External tritium purchase at $30k/g destroys FOAK economics.
Wall replacement frequency drives amortized opex.
Low duty cycle inflates LCOE proportionally.
REBCO tape supply gates magnet manufacturing throughput.
Li-6 + Be supply gates blanket manufacturing.
Licensing duration enters cost of capital.
Skilled operations labor is a cost lever at scale.
Without economics, grid integration is moot.

risks.name: Global tritium inventory shortfall
risks.description: Commercial tritium inventory (~25 kg, CANDU byproduct) is far below FOAK plant needs. If breeding fails, plants stall.
risks.mitigations: Test blanket modules at ITER (2035+); accelerated breeder R&D at private companies (CFS, Helion alternative fuels).
risks.source_title: IAEA — fusion fuel cycle & tritium inventory

risks.name: FOAK plant cost overruns
risks.description: ITER's $20B+ overrun pattern repeats in commercial FOAK plants; investor capital dries up.
risks.mitigations: Fixed-price contracting; small-plant strategies (CFS, Helion); diversified investor base (sovereign + corporate).
risks.source_title: DOE FES — Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program

risks.name: First-wall failure modes at scale
risks.description: Helium production, swelling, and embrittlement under 14 MeV neutron flux may force shorter replacement cycles than designed.
risks.mitigations: Materials irradiation testing (IFMIF-DONES); liquid-wall alternatives; modular wall design for fast swaps.
risks.source_title: arXiv — first-wall materials under DT neutron load

risks.name: Anti-nuclear policy drag
risks.description: Public confusion conflating fusion with fission could drive permitting delays in some jurisdictions, even with clear NRC framework.
risks.mitigations: Communications campaigns emphasizing zero long-lived waste; siting in pro-energy jurisdictions (Texas, UK, Korea).

risks.name: REBCO supplier concentration
risks.description: REBCO tape supply is concentrated across 4-5 vendors; any disruption (geopolitics, IP litigation) stalls magnet production globally.
risks.mitigations: Multi-source qualification at each fusion company; Faraday + AMSC US capacity expansions.

risks.name: Alternative clean baseload outpaces fusion
risks.description: SMRs (small modular fission), enhanced geothermal, or long-duration storage may capture the clean-baseload market before fusion ships.
risks.mitigations: Fusion's positioning shifts to niches (industrial heat, no-water siting); accelerated commercialization timeline.
